Winch Actuation (Forward/Reverse): Proportional solenoids shift the main spool. Regulated pressure flows from the P rail, through the compensator, and out to either port A or B to drive the bidirectional winch motor. Return flow from the opposite port routes back through the spool to the T rail. The LS shuttle valve resolves the highest working pressure and sends it to the LS rail.
Overpressure / Shock Protection: If external forces cause pressure in port A or B to exceed the relief threshold, the respective port relief valve opens to dump excess fluid directly to the T rail.
Anti-cavitation: If a vacuum or negative pressure condition occurs in port A or B (e.g., motor overrunning), the check valve draws makeup fluid from the T rail into the work port.

flow_scenarios: Extension: Fluid from P flows through the compensator and main spool, then through the counterbalance check valve directly to the cap ends of both cylinders. Return fluid from the rod ends combines via the flow divider (20), passes through the counterbalance valve (piloted open by cap-end pressure), and returns to T via the main spool.

Retraction: Fluid from P flows through the compensator and main spool, then through the counterbalance check valve and splits equally via the flow divider (20) to the rod ends of both cylinders. Return fluid from the cap ends passes through the counterbalance valve (piloted open by rod-end pressure) and returns to T via the main spool.
Neutral/Load Holding: Main spool is centered, blocking A and B ports. The dual counterbalance valve (18) closes, locking fluid in both ends of the cylinders to mechanically hold the load.
Overload: If pressure on A or B exceeds the set limit, the respective port relief valve opens to dump fluid to the T rail.

energized B (release cylinder): Spool connects P to B' and A' to T. Pressure builds in the dead-ended B' line, sending a pilot signal to open the counterbalance valve. Actuated (e.g., A port pressurized): Flow from P passes through the pressure compensator and main spool to work port A. Anti-cavitation: If pressure in port A or B drops below tank pressure, the check valve integrated with the port relief opens to draw makeup fluid from the T line into the work port.
